text:
maria: heads-up, several model-worker pods are stuck Pending in eu-west-1, scheduler says Fit failure: Insufficient allocatable nvidia.com/gpu (or fragmentation). Not seeing autoscaler spin up more nodes. :confused:
jon: can you paste the pod yaml / resource requests?
maria: sure, here's the resources block from one of the pods:
```yaml
resources:
  requests:
    cpu: "4"
    memory: "16Gi"
    nvidia.com/gpu: "0.25"
  limits:
    nvidia.com/gpu: "1"
```
jon: ah, 0.25 GPU request. We're running mixed nodepools (a100-pool, t4-mig-pool, g4-standard) — only the t4 nodes have MIG enabled. CA might be refusing to create new nodes because the nodegroup selector doesn't match the fractional-gpu capability.
kai: CA logs? sometimes expander/scale-up logic decides no nodegroup would help because it assumes whole-gpu packing.
arjun: posted CA log excerpt from last scale attempt:
```
I0101 12:34:56 cluster_autoscaler.go:xxxx] No candidate node group found for pod model-worker-abc: reasons: Pod requires resource nvidia.com/gpu fractional but node group 'a100-pool' not mig-enabled; 'g4-standard' has no spare slots; 't4-mig-pool' max nodes reached.
```
maria: t4 pool is at max (3/3) because of budget cap, a100 pool accepts whole GPUs only, g4 nodes already fragmented with lots of 0.5 requests.
jon: quick checks: are those pods tolerating any taints? do they require specific labels? maybe some affinity is blocking CA from choosing a nodegroup.
kai: also check Device Plugin versions. If plugin doesn't advertise 'nvidia.com/gpu' as schedulable fractional resource, scheduler will refuse packing.
arjun: action item: lower priority pods can be preempted but these are production. Two options: 1) temporarily increase t4-mig-pool max to allow scale up, 2) change pod requests to 1 GPU (coarser) so CA will pick a100 nodes, 3) enable fractional scheduling on a100 nodes via MIG if supported.
maria: we can't MIG a100 quickly. Ops approval needed to bump t4 pool cap. Cost team OK with short burst if we annotate.
jon: another intermediate measure: set cluster-autoscaler expander to least-waste and enable balance-similar-node-groups to prefer t4-mig-pool for small requests. That might force CA to try t4 nodes first.
kai: also noticed kube-scheduler profile has 'EnableVolumeScheduling' and custom predicates; can we relax PodTopologyConstraints for these workers? they had topologySpreadConstraints for gpu-type which prevents cross-pool packing.
arjun: here's a small one-liner to find fragmented nodes:
```bash
kubectl get nodes -o json | jq -r '.items[] | {name:.metadata.name, allocatable:.status.allocatable, pods:.status.capacity}' | head -n 20
```
maria: I've opened a ticket to temporarily raise t4 pool limit and removed the strict topologySpread on the deployment. Applying change now. :nerd_face:
deploy-bot: Scaling nodegroup t4-mig-pool from 3 -> 5 (request by maria). ETA ~5m.
srebot: FYI, CA will only register new nodes after cloud provider reports they are ready; watch for Kubelet registration failures (IAM/instance-profile often the culprit).
jon: once nodes are up, we should run a small job to simulate packing: create 6 pods request 0.25 gpu and confirm they densify on t4 MIG slices. If they still scatter, device-plugin config mismatch.
kai: noted. if any pods still Pending after scale, drop a /describe here and I'll dig into scheduler decisions. :eyes:
